title: Grouping Values
goal: Put related values under one name, and build one.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1 Afternoon: User-Defined Types

sections.text: A struct groups several values under one name. You will know the idea as a struct in C or Go, or as a small class with no inheritance.

sections.caption: Every field is named and typed.

sections.text: When you build one you must fill in every field. Rust has no half-built value and no implicit null, so leaving one out is error `E0063`.
You read a field with a dot, the same as in most languages. Writing to one needs the binding to be `mut`.

sections.caption: Reading is free. Writing needs mut.

sections.text: When most fields come from an existing value, `..base` fills in the rest. It has to come last, and it consumes `base` unless every field it copies is a simple value.

sections.caption: age is new, name comes from u.

explanation: Put related values under one name, and build one.
